newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh deputies demand end to Russian weapons tests.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh deputies demand end to Russian weapons tests.

text.p: Kazakh parliamentary deputies said on Wednesday they had demanded that the government review an agreement with neighbouring Russia allowing it continued use of weapons test sites in the former Soviet republic.

"We sent a statement (on Tuesday) to (President Nursultan) Nazarbayev demanding a review and parliamentary hearing on use of the test sites," Sharip Omarov, chairman of parliament's Committee for International Affairs, Defence and Security, told Reuters. "If it came to a vote, I do not think this agreement would be ratified," he said.

The Russian and Kazakh governments signed an agreement in Moscow last October allowing the Russian defence ministry continued use of four test sites for conventional weapons in the vast Central Asian nation's central steppe land.

But Omarov said the agreement had yet to be ratified and the majority of deputies in both the upper and lower houses of the Kazakh parliament had serious "ecological, social and political concerns" over continued weapons testing by Russia in the republic.

"All the deputies are against this," said influential opposition deputy Zamanbek Nurkadilov. "Kazakhstan wants to be a neutral country and it's given up its own nuclear weapons so Russia's use of the test sites makes no sense," he said.

Kazakhstan was the first former Soviet republic to ship its nuclear missiles back to Russia. Some of it 16.9 million population are still suffering from the after-effects of decades of nuclear tests at its Semipalatinsk nuclear test site in the northeast of the republic.
Tests at Semipalatinsk have now been halted.
